explanation: Mild public affection — holding hands, a hug, or a quick kiss — is common and accepted in Italy, much like in most of Western Europe. More passionate or prolonged displays can draw disapproving looks in conservative settings or around family, more because Italians value composure in public than because of any strict rule against affection itself.
local_tip: Keep it to hand-holding or a brief kiss in public, and save anything more intimate for private settings.
regional_note: Older generations and smaller, more traditional towns in the south tend to be less comfortable with public affection than younger people in big northern cities.

also_check.note: Passionate public affection can still violate public decency laws and lead to fines, even after 2020 reforms loosened rules on cohabitation and alcohol.
Cheek-kiss greetings and light PDA are common and socially accepted.
Public affection beyond hand-holding is uncommon and can draw stares, though it's seen as awkward rather than offensive.
